taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla (now P. hastata): a perennial 2 dm to 5 dm tall from a branched caudex.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: a perennial from a branched caudex.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: lower leaves with petioles about equalling the blade, the stem leaves reduced upwards.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: lower leaves 3 cm to 10 cm long, 0.5 cm to 2.5 cm broad.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: the petiole slender, about equalling the blade; the upper stem leaves reduced, so set from 0.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: lower leaves linear-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: leaves mostly entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: canescent and appressed-hirsute, the foliage silvery: drawn as silky.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: flowers numerous in dense, paniculate or racemose cymes.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: the cymes 2 cm to 10 cm long, erect in fruit.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 15 to 40 flowers and buds in a dense coiled cluster, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 292543246, 7010334, 88338300, 147226465, 224829642, 214097469, 93149500, 244692140): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Five equal corolla lobes: a regular flower, set by hand from iNaturalist photos of flowering plants (observations 292543246, 7010334, 88338300, 147226465, 224829642, 214097469, 93149500, 244692140): the flora gives no count or measure.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: corolla 4 mm to 6 mm long, 5 mm to 6 mm broad: open bell-shaped.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: corolla 4 mm to 6 mm long, 5 mm to 6 mm broad.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: corolla white to lavender; drawn dull white, as in most of the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: capsule ovoid, 3 mm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 500, Phacelia leucophylla: flowering June to July.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: silvery grey-green, hairy stems and leaves with deep veins; dense coiled clusters of dull white flowers bristling with long stamens.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for silverleaf phacelia from Abrams's description and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). Its inflorescence is drawn as one cluster at each stem's tip, sized by the traits, so the stem ends where the cluster begins. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.38 m tall at 3 years in the open, within the flora's range. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
